Find $|r\left(\frac{\pi }{3}\right)|$ given that $r(t)=⟨2\operatorname{cos}t,\,4\operatorname{sin}t,\,6⟩.$

Evaluating the function at $t=\frac{\pi }{3},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\left(\frac{\pi }{3}\right) & =\left\langle 2\operatorname{cos}\left(\frac{\pi }{3}\right),\,4\operatorname{sin}\left(\frac{\pi }{3}\right),\,6\right\rangle  \\  & =\left\langle 2\cdot \frac{1}{2},\,4\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},\,6\right\rangle  \\  & =⟨1,\,2\sqrt{3},\,6⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the magnitude of this vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|r\left(\frac{\pi }{3}\right)| & =\sqrt{{(1)}^{2}+{(2\sqrt{3})}^{2}+(6)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+12+36} \\  & =\sqrt{49} \\  & =7.\end{aligned}
$$

\begin{aligned}r(3) & =\left\langle \sqrt{\frac{12}{3+1}},\,{3}^{2}-8\right\rangle  \\  & =\left\langle \sqrt{\frac{12}{4}},\,1\right\rangle  \\  & =⟨\sqrt{3},\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the magnitude of this vector, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}|r(3)| & =\sqrt{{(\sqrt{3})}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{3+1} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem: Find the value of the vector function $\mathbf f(t) = \left\langle \cos t, \: \sin t, \: t \right\rangle$ at $t = \pi.$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
To evaluate, we substitute $t = \pi$ into the function, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(\pi ) & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi ,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ,\,\pi ⟩=⟨-1,0,\pi \,⟩\end{aligned}
$$

So, the value of $\mathbf f (t)$ at $t = \pi$ is $\langle -1, 0, \pi \rangle.$

We can also express the answer using $\mathbf i$-$\mathbf j$-$\mathbf k$ notation or square bracket notation, as follows:
$$
-\,\mathbf i +\pi\,\mathbf k, \qquad  {\left[ \begin{array}{c}- 1 \\ 0 \\ \pi \end{array} \right]}
$$
